title: Public Assets and the Publish Step

hints.text: Resources/Public/ of an installed package is published into the document root by the Composer installer, as a symlink below _assets/<hash>/. The hash is the package, not the file.

That publishing happens when the packages are installed, not at runtime. A file added to Resources/Public/ afterwards is not resolvable until they are installed again, and the remedy is a Composer install rather than a cache flush.

TYPO3 publishes Resources/Public/ itself, below _assets/<hash>/ in the document root: the asset:publish command, which composer install runs on its own, extension:setup, and activating an extension. TYPO3_SKIP_ASSET_PUBLISH=1 keeps composer install out of it, and $GLOBALS['TYPO3_CONF_VARS']['SYS']['SystemResources']['filesystemPublishingType'] chooses between linking the folder and copying it — 'mirror' is what a read-only or container deployment needs. Where it linked, a file added afterwards is served straight away; where it copied, asset:publish is what picks it up, and never a cache flush.

Which paths of a package are addressable is declared rather than assumed. The default is Configuration, Resources/Private and Resources/Public, and a public folder or single file anywhere else — a Build output directory, say — is published and resolvable only once Configuration/Resources.php names it. That file is evaluated without TYPO3 booted, so nothing global is available in it.
The failure has a name: CanNotResolvePublicResourceException, thrown for a path that plainly exists on disk.
Nothing throws here — PathUtility computes the URL from the path either way — so the symptom is an asset that 404s in the browser rather than an exception in PHP.

In PHP the URL comes from the System Resource API: inject SystemResourceFactory, call createPublicResource() with the identifier — PKG:<composer name>:<path in the package>, EXT:<key>/<path>, FAL:<storage uid>:/<identifier> or a URL — and hand the result to SystemResourcePublisherInterface::generateUri(). Both are injectable, and replacing the publisher is how a CDN gets its own URIs. They live in TYPO3\CMS\Core\SystemResource: the factory directly below it, the publisher interface and UriGenerationOptions below its Publishing namespace. The migration example in the changelog entry that deprecated the old way imports all three from TYPO3\CMS\Core\Resource instead, where none of them is.
PathUtility::getPublicResourceWebPath() is what computes such a URL here.

PathUtility::getPublicResourceWebPath() still exists and still resolves such a path, and it is the way out rather than the way in: it is deprecated here, every call raises E_USER_DEPRECATED, and the next major has removed it.

PathUtility::getSystemResourceUri() sits beside it in the same class and is a third thing: neither the supported route nor the deprecated one. Its docblock marks it @internal and announces its removal, or its becoming private, before this major reaches LTS — which has not happened yet, so the signature reads as current API and is not one. It is there so the core can migrate its own call sites. Extension code calling it is a finding rather than a static shorthand, and the factory and the publisher above are the whole of what is offered.

_assets_install/ is the sibling directory that publishing writes, and a reader who has just learned about _assets/ has no reason to suspect it. It is the same publishing done from the failsafe container the install tool boots, so it holds that container's packages and not the rest, and the same asset:publish run produces both.

hints: The hash is md5 of the package directory's path relative to the project root, with the slash on both ends: /vendor/<vendor>/<name>/ for a package Composer installed. The same layout on another machine yields the same hash, and a package that moves between vendor/ and packages/ gets a new one.

hints.text: A folder Configuration/Resources.php declares beside Resources/Public hashes the same relative path with the declared folder appended, so each declared folder publishes under a prefix of its own.

hints: Reference such a file as EXT:<key>/Resources/Public/... and let the resolver produce the published URI. The _assets path is an implementation detail and its hash changes with the layout.

What publishing writes into the document root is generated and is not committed. The rest of what a Composer installation puts there, and the ignore file that is read off it, is project-build-and-scripts.

title: Building Assets in a Project Extension
hints: An extension owns its asset source, build tool and generated output; installing it into TYPO3 does not attach its Sass or TypeScript to the core's Build/Sources pipelines. Put only browser-consumable output below Resources/Public/ and keep the source where the extension's own package scripts name it.

Decide whether generated assets are committed. If they are, source and output change together; if they are not, the project deployment has to run the build. The extension's package.json and CI are the executable record of that decision.

The public-assets hint covers how Resources/Public files are published and referenced. The extension-declarative-files hint covers Configuration/JavaScriptModules.php for backend JavaScript import maps; neither implies a particular bundler.

For a patch to the TYPO3 backend itself, css-source-build-boundaries and backend-typescript describe the core's source trees and generated pairs; those paths and commands do not transfer to an extension.
